mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive quarters in at least 5 out of 6 test windows.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household income and spending power, which dampens corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 mean excess return) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer and business confidence, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months in at least 4 out of 6 test windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening cycle, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months in at least 3 out of 5 test windows.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (implied via RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and RSAFS > 12-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.10 mean excess return) during periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages for at least three consecutive months in at least 4 out of 6 test windows.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) during periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months in at least 3 out of 5 test windows.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS) below its 5-year minimum indicates constrained household balance sheets, which reduces discretionary spending and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < 5-year minimum for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 mean excess return) during periods when RSAFS falls below its 5-year minimum for three consecutive months in at least 4 out of 6 test windows.
